title: A quadratic-density lower bound for tetrahedral cylinder covers
description: Let T be a regular tetrahedron and let A_min(T) be the least area of an orthogonal projection of T onto a plane. We prove that every finite cover of T by cylinders with measurable perpendicular bases B_i satisfies sum_i |B_i| >= (sqrt(15)/9) A_min(T). The proof computes the largest line integral of a radial quadratic density on T. We also prove that sqrt(15)/9 is the best constant obtainable from any nonnegative polynomial density of degree at most two by dividing its mass by a uniform bound on its line integrals. This optimality concerns the density method within that class, rather than the cylinder-covering infimum.

references.reference: K. Bezdek and A. E. Litvak, Covering convex bodies by cylinders and lattice points by flats, Journal of Geometric Analysis 19 (2009), no. 2, 233-243. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12220-008-9063-6.
K. Bezdek and A. E. Litvak, Packing convex bodies by cylinders, Discrete & Computational Geometry 55 (2016), no. 3, 725-738. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-016-9760-z.
